title: अंश २ · अध्याय १

items.speaker: मैत्रेय उवाच
items.text:
भगवन् सम्यागाख्यातं ममैतदखिलं त्वया ।
जगतः सर्गसम्बन्घि यत् पृष्टोऽसि गुरो मया ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
bhagavan samyāgākhyātaṃ mamaitadakhilaṃ tvayā |
jagataḥ sargasambanghi yat pṛṣṭo'si guro mayā || 1 ||

items.text:
योऽयमंशो जगत्सृष्टिसम्बद्धो गदितस्त्वया ।
तत्राहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि भूयोऽपि मुनिसत्तम ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
yo'yamaṃśo jagatsṛṣṭisambaddho gaditastvayā |
tatrāhaṃ śrotumicchāmi bhūyo'pi munisattama || 2 ||

items.text:
प्रियव्रतोत्तानपादौ सुतौ स्वायम्भुवस्य यौ ।
तयोरुत्तानपादस्य ध्रुवः पुत्रस्त्वयोदितः ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
priyavratottānapādau sutau svāyambhuvasya yau |
tayoruttānapādasya dhruvaḥ putrastvayoditaḥ || 3 ||

items.text:
प्रियव्रतस्य नैवोक्ता भवता द्विज सन्ततिः ।
तामहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि प्रसन्नो वक्तुमर्हसि ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
priyavratasya naivoktā bhavatā dvija santatiḥ |
tāmahaṃ śrotumicchāmi prasanno vaktumarhasi || 4 ||

items.speaker: पराशार उवाच
items.text:
कर्द्दमस्यात्मजां कन्यामुपयेमे प्रियव्रतः ।
सम्राट् कुक्षी च तत्कन्ये दश पुत्रास्तथापरे ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
karddamasyātmajāṃ kanyāmupayeme priyavrataḥ |
samrāṭ kukṣī ca tatkanye daśa putrāstathāpare || 5 ||

items.text:
महाप्राज्ञा महावीर्य्या विनीता दयिताः पितुः ।
प्रियव्रतसुताः ख्यातास्तेषां नामानि मे श्वृणु ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
mahāprājñā mahāvīryyā vinītā dayitāḥ pituḥ |
priyavratasutāḥ khyātāsteṣāṃ nāmāni me śvṛṇu || 6 ||

items.text:
आग्नीध्रश्चाग्निबाहुश्च वपुष्मान् द्युतिमांस्तथा ।
मेधा मेधातिथिर्भव्यः सवनः पुत्र एव च ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
āgnīdhraścāgnibāhuśca vapuṣmān dyutimāṃstathā |
medhā medhātithirbhavyaḥ savanaḥ putra eva ca || 7 ||

items.text:
ज्योतिष्मान् दशमस्तेषां सत्यनामा सुतोऽभवत् ।
प्रियव्रतस्य पुत्रास्तु प्रख्याता बलवीर्य्यतः ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
jyotiṣmān daśamasteṣāṃ satyanāmā suto'bhavat |
priyavratasya putrāstu prakhyātā balavīryyataḥ || 8 ||

items.text:
मेधाग्निबाहुपुत्रास्तु त्रयो योगपरायणाः ।
जातिस्मरा महाभाग न राज्याय मनो दधुः ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
medhāgnibāhuputrāstu trayo yogaparāyaṇāḥ |
jātismarā mahābhāga na rājyāya mano dadhuḥ || 9 ||

items.text:
निर्म्मलाः सर्वकालन्तु समस्तार्थेषु वै मुने ।
चक्रुः क्रिया यथान्यायमफलाकाङ्क्षिणो हि ते ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
nirmmalāḥ sarvakālantu samastārtheṣu vai mune |
cakruḥ kriyā yathānyāyamaphalākāṅkṣiṇo hi te || 10 ||

items.text:
प्रियव्रतो ददौ तेषां सप्तानां मुनिसत्तम !
विभज्य सप्त द्वीपानि मैत्रेय सुमहात्मनाम् ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
priyavrato dadau teṣāṃ saptānāṃ munisattama !
vibhajya sapta dvīpāni maitreya sumahātmanām || 11 ||

items.text:
जम्बूद्वीपं महाभाग सोऽग्नीध्राय ददौ पिता ।
मेधातिथेस्तथा प्रादात् प्लक्षद्वीपमथापरम् ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
jambūdvīpaṃ mahābhāga so'gnīdhrāya dadau pitā |
medhātithestathā prādāt plakṣadvīpamathāparam || 12 ||

items.text:
शाल्मले च वपुष्मन्तं नरेन्द्रमभिषिक्तवान् ।
ज्योतिष्मन्तं कुशद्रीपे राजानं कृतवान् प्रभुः ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
śālmale ca vapuṣmantaṃ narendramabhiṣiktavān |
jyotiṣmantaṃ kuśadrīpe rājānaṃ kṛtavān prabhuḥ || 13 ||

items.text:
द्युतिमन्तं च राजानं क्रौञ्चद्रीपे समादिशत् ।
शाकद्वीपेश्वरञ्चापि भव्यञ्चक्रे च स प्रभुः ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
dyutimantaṃ ca rājānaṃ krauñcadrīpe samādiśat |
śākadvīpeśvarañcāpi bhavyañcakre ca sa prabhuḥ || 14 ||

items.text: सवनं पुष्करद्वीपे राजानं समकारयत ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr: savanaṃ puṣkaradvīpe rājānaṃ samakārayata || 15 ||

items.text:
जम्बूद्वीपेश्वरो यस्तु आग्नीध्रो मुनिसत्तम ।
तस्य पुत्रा बभुवुस्ते प्रजापतिसमा नव ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
jambūdvīpeśvaro yastu āgnīdhro munisattama |
tasya putrā babhuvuste prajāpatisamā nava || 16 ||

items.text:
नाभिः किम्पुरुषश्वे वै हरिवर्ष इलावृतः ।
रम्यो हिरण्वान् षष्ठश्च कुरुर्भद्राश्व एव च ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
nābhiḥ kimpuruṣaśve vai harivarṣa ilāvṛtaḥ |
ramyo hiraṇvān ṣaṣṭhaśca kururbhadrāśva eva ca || 17 ||

items.text:
केतुमालस्तथैवान्यः साधुचेष्टो नृपोऽभवत् ।
जम्बूद्रीपविभागांश्च तषां विप्र निशामय ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
ketumālastathaivānyaḥ sādhuceṣṭo nṛpo'bhavat |
jambūdrīpavibhāgāṃśca taṣāṃ vipra niśāmaya || 18 ||

items.text:
पित्रा दत्तं हिमाह्वन्तु वर्षं नाभेस्तु दक्षिणम् ।
हेमकूटं तथा वर्षं ददौ किम्पुरुषाय सः ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
pitrā dattaṃ himāhvantu varṣaṃ nābhestu dakṣiṇam |
hemakūṭaṃ tathā varṣaṃ dadau kimpuruṣāya saḥ || 19 ||

items.text:
तृतीयं नैषधं वर्षं हरिवर्षाय दत्तवान ।
इलावृताय प्रददौ मैरुर्यत्र तु मध्यगः ॥ २० ॥
items.tr:
tṛtīyaṃ naiṣadhaṃ varṣaṃ harivarṣāya dattavāna |
ilāvṛtāya pradadau mairuryatra tu madhyagaḥ || 20 ||

items.text:
नीलाचलाश्वितं वर्षं रम्याय प्रददौ पिता ।
श्वेतं तदुत्तरं वर्षं पित्रा दत्तं हिरण्वते ॥ २१ ॥
items.tr:
nīlācalāśvitaṃ varṣaṃ ramyāya pradadau pitā |
śvetaṃ taduttaraṃ varṣaṃ pitrā dattaṃ hiraṇvate || 21 ||

items.text:
यदुत्तरं श्वृङ्गवतो वर्षं तत् कुरवे ददौ ।
मेरोः पूर्व्वेणा यद् वर्षं भद्राश्वाय प्रदत्तवान् ॥ २२ ॥
items.tr:
yaduttaraṃ śvṛṅgavato varṣaṃ tat kurave dadau |
meroḥ pūrvveṇā yad varṣaṃ bhadrāśvāya pradattavān || 22 ||

items.text:
गन्धमादनवर्षन्तु केतुमालाय दत्तवान ।
इत्येतानि ददौ तेभ्यः पुत्रेभ्यः स नरेश्वरः ॥ २३ ॥
items.tr:
gandhamādanavarṣantu ketumālāya dattavāna |
ityetāni dadau tebhyaḥ putrebhyaḥ sa nareśvaraḥ || 23 ||

items.text:
वर्षेष्वेतेषु तान् पुत्रानभिषितच्य स भूमिपः ।
शालग्रामं महापुण्यं मैत्रेय तपसे ययौ ॥ २४ ॥
items.tr:
varṣeṣveteṣu tān putrānabhiṣitacya sa bhūmipaḥ |
śālagrāmaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ maitreya tapase yayau || 24 ||

items.text:
यानि किंपुरुषादीनि वर्षाण्यष्टौ महामुने।
तेषां स्वाभाविकी सिद्धिः सुखप्राया ह्ययत्नतः ॥ २५ ॥
items.tr:
yāni kiṃpuruṣādīni varṣāṇyaṣṭau mahāmune|
teṣāṃ svābhāvikī siddhiḥ sukhaprāyā hyayatnataḥ || 25 ||

items.text:
विपर्य्ययो न तेष्वस्ति जरामृत्युभयं न च ।
धर्म्माधर्म्मौ न तेष्वास्तां नोत्तमाधममध्यमाः ॥ २६ ॥
items.tr:
viparyyayo na teṣvasti jarāmṛtyubhayaṃ na ca |
dharmmādharmmau na teṣvāstāṃ nottamādhamamadhyamāḥ || 26 ||

items.text:
न तेष्वस्ति युगावस्था क्षेत्रेष्वष्टासु सर्व्वदा ।
हिमाह्वयं तु वै वर्षं नाभेरासीन्महात्मनः ॥ २७ ॥
items.tr:
na teṣvasti yugāvasthā kṣetreṣvaṣṭāsu sarvvadā |
himāhvayaṃ tu vai varṣaṃ nābherāsīnmahātmanaḥ || 27 ||

items.text:
तस्यर्षभोऽभवत् पुत्रो मेरुदेव्यां महाद्युतिः ।
ऋषभाद् भरतो जज्ञ ज्येष्ठःपुत्रशतस्य सः ॥ २८ ॥
items.tr:
tasyarṣabho'bhavat putro merudevyāṃ mahādyutiḥ |
ṛṣabhād bharato jajña jyeṣṭhaḥputraśatasya saḥ || 28 ||

items.text:
कृत्वा राज्यं स्वधर्म्मेण तथेष्ट्वा विविधान् मखान् ।
अभिषच्य सुतं ज्येष्ठं भरतं पृथिवीपतिम् ॥ २९ ॥
items.tr:
kṛtvā rājyaṃ svadharmmeṇa tatheṣṭvā vividhān makhān |
abhiṣacya sutaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ bharataṃ pṛthivīpatim || 29 ||

items.text:
तपसे स महाभागः पुलस्त्यस्याश्रमं ययौ ।
वानप्रस्थविधानेन तत्रापि कृतनिश्चयः ॥ ३० ॥
items.tr:
tapase sa mahābhāgaḥ pulastyasyāśramaṃ yayau |
vānaprasthavidhānena tatrāpi kṛtaniścayaḥ || 30 ||

items.text:
तपस्तेपे यथान्यायं यदा च स महीपतिः ।
तपसा कर्शितोऽत्यर्थं कृशो धमनिसन्ततः ॥ ३१ ॥
items.tr:
tapastepe yathānyāyaṃ yadā ca sa mahīpatiḥ |
tapasā karśito'tyarthaṃ kṛśo dhamanisantataḥ || 31 ||

items.text:
नग्नो वीटां मुखे दत्त्वा वीराध्वानं ततो गतः ।
ततश्च भारतं वर्षमेतल्लोकेषु गीयते ॥ ३२ ॥
items.tr:
nagno vīṭāṃ mukhe dattvā vīrādhvānaṃ tato gataḥ |
tataśca bhārataṃ varṣametallokeṣu gīyate || 32 ||

items.text:
भरताय यतः पित्रा दत्तं प्रातिष्ठता वनम् ।
सुमतिर्भरतस्याभूत् पुत्रः परमधार्म्मिकः ॥ ३३ ॥
items.tr:
bharatāya yataḥ pitrā dattaṃ prātiṣṭhatā vanam |
sumatirbharatasyābhūt putraḥ paramadhārmmikaḥ || 33 ||

items.text:
कृत्वा सम्यग् ददौ तस्मै राज्यमिष्टमखः पिता ।
पुत्रसंक्रमितश्रीस्तु भरतः स महीपतिः ॥ ३४ ॥
items.tr:
kṛtvā samyag dadau tasmai rājyamiṣṭamakhaḥ pitā |
putrasaṃkramitaśrīstu bharataḥ sa mahīpatiḥ || 34 ||

items.text:
योगाभ्यासरतः प्राणान् शालग्रामेऽत्यजन्मुने ।
अजायत च विप्रोऽसौ योगिनां प्रवरे कुले ॥ ३५ ॥
items.tr:
yogābhyāsarataḥ prāṇān śālagrāme'tyajanmune |
ajāyata ca vipro'sau yogināṃ pravare kule || 35 ||

items.text:
मैत्रय । तस्य चरितं कथयिष्यामि ते पुनः ।
सुमतेस्तेजसस्तस्मादिन्द्रद्युम्नो व्यजायत ॥ ३६ ॥
items.tr:
maitraya | tasya caritaṃ kathayiṣyāmi te punaḥ |
sumatestejasastasmādindradyumno vyajāyata || 36 ||

items.text:
परमेष्ठी ततस्तस्मात् प्रतिहारस्तदन्वयः ।
प्रतिहर्त्तेति विख्यात उत्पन्नस्तस्य चात्मजः ॥ ३७ ॥
items.tr:
parameṣṭhī tatastasmāt pratihārastadanvayaḥ |
pratihartteti vikhyāta utpannastasya cātmajaḥ || 37 ||

items.text:
भुवस्तस्मात् तथोद्गीथः प्रस्तारस्तत्सुतो विभुः ।
पृथुस्ततोऽभवन्नक्तो नक्तस्यापि गयः सुतः ॥ ३८ ॥
items.tr:
bhuvastasmāt tathodgīthaḥ prastārastatsuto vibhuḥ |
pṛthustato'bhavannakto naktasyāpi gayaḥ sutaḥ || 38 ||

items.text:
नरो गयस्य तनयस्तत्पुत्रोऽभूद् विराट् ततः ।
तस्य पुत्रो महावीर्य्यो धीमांस्तस्मादजायत ॥ ३९ ॥
items.tr:
naro gayasya tanayastatputro'bhūd virāṭ tataḥ |
tasya putro mahāvīryyo dhīmāṃstasmādajāyata || 39 ||

items.text:
महान्तस्तत्सुतश्चाभूनूमनस्युस्तस्य चात्मजः ।
त्वष्टा त्वष्टुश्च विरजो रजस्तस्याप्यभूत् सुतः ॥ ४० ॥
items.tr:
mahāntastatsutaścābhūnūmanasyustasya cātmajaḥ |
tvaṣṭā tvaṣṭuśca virajo rajastasyāpyabhūt sutaḥ || 40 ||

items.text:
शतजिद्रजसस्तस्य जज्ञ पुत्रशतं मनने ।
विशगूज्योतिःप्रधानास्ते यैरिमा वर्द्धिताः प्रजाः ॥ ४१ ॥
items.tr:
śatajidrajasastasya jajña putraśataṃ manane |
viśagūjyotiḥpradhānāste yairimā varddhitāḥ prajāḥ || 41 ||

items.text:
तैरिदं भारतं वर्षं नवभेदमलङ्गतम ।
तेषां वंशप्रसूतैश्च भुक्तेयें भारती पुरा ॥ ४२ ॥
items.tr:
tairidaṃ bhārataṃ varṣaṃ navabhedamalaṅgatama |
teṣāṃ vaṃśaprasūtaiśca bhukteyeṃ bhāratī purā || 42 ||

items.text: कृतत्रेतादिसर्गेण युगाख्या ह्म क्सप्ततिः ॥ ४३ ॥
items.tr: kṛtatretādisargeṇa yugākhyā hma ksaptatiḥ || 43 ||

items.text:
एष स्वायम्भुवः सर्गो येनेदं पूरितं जगत् ।
वाराहे तु मुने ! कल्पे पूर्वमन्वान्तराधिपः ॥ ४४ ॥
items.tr:
eṣa svāyambhuvaḥ sargo yenedaṃ pūritaṃ jagat |
vārāhe tu mune ! kalpe pūrvamanvāntarādhipaḥ || 44 ||

en_chapter: Maitreya said:—"O venerable Sir, O preceptor, you have fully described unto me all that I asked you regarding the creation of the universe. But there is a portion of this subject, O foremost of ascetics, which I desire to hear again. Pryavrata and Uttanapada were the two sons of Swayambhuva Manu and you related to me the story of Dhruva, the son of Uttanapada. But, O twice-born one, you did not mention the progeny of Pryavrata and I wish to hear from you an account of his family". Parāçara said:—Prayvrata married Kanya, the daughter of Kardama, and had by her two daughters named Samrat and Kukshi and ten sons, wise, valiant, humble, obedient to their father; named Agnidhra, Agnivāhu, Vapushmat, Dyutimat, Medha, Bhabya, Savalā, Putra. And the tenth of them was Jyotishman; and the significance of this name was made good by him. All the sons of Pryavrata were celebrated for strength and prowess. Of these three, Medha, Agnivāhu and Putra, were given up to religious devotion. And those high-souled ones remembering the actions of their pristine births, did not wish for kingdom. And they diligently and in due time practised the rites of austerities, wholly disinterested and expecting no reward. O Maitreya, O foremost of Munis, Pryavrata conferred the seven islands upon his seven illustrious sons. The father conferred upon Agnidhra the sovereignty of Jamvudwipa; to Medhathiti he gave Plakshadwipa: he made Vapushmat the sovereign over the Dwipa of Salmali: and appointed Jyotishmat, king of Kusadwipa: he made Dutimat the king of Kraunchdwipa, Bhabya the king of Sakadwipa and Savala the sovereign of the Dwipa of Pushkara.

O foremost of Munis, Agnidhra, the king of Jamvudwipa had nine sons, all equal to the patriarchs in prowess.—Nābhi, Kimpurasha, Harwarsha, Ilāvrita, Ramya, Hiranvat, Kuru, Bhadraswa and Ketumala, who was a prince ever devoted to the practice of piety.

Hear next, O Brahman, from me how he divided Jamvudwipa amongst his sons. He conferred on Nabhi the country called Hima, south of Himavān or snowy mountains. And he gave to Kimpurusha the country of Himakuta and to Harivarsha the country of Nishada. And he bestowed upon Ilāvrita the country in the centre of which mount Meru is situated. And he conferred upon Kamya the countries lying between it and the Nila mountain. He gave to Hiravat the country lying to the north of it. He gave to Kuru the country bounded by Sringavar. He gave to Bhadraswa the countries situate on the east of Meru and he gave to Ketumala Gandhamadana which was situate on the west of it. Thus that lord of men, conferred the various portions of his kingdom, upon his sons. And having installed his sons as kings of diverse regions that lord of earth retired to the holy place of pilgrimage Salagrama and engaged in penance, O Maitreya.

O great Muni, the eight countries, Kintpurusha and others are places of perfect enjoyment and spontaneous happiness. In those countries there is no viccissitude of circumstances, no fear of decrepitude or death, no distinction of virtue and vice, better or worse. Nor in these eight countries are to be seen the effects wrought by the cycle of ages.

The high-souled Nabhi, who had obtained the country of Nimahwa as his kingdom, had by his queen Meru, the highly effulgent son Rishabha; and who had again a hundred sons, the eldest of whom was Bharata. Having ruled over the kingdom piously and performed many sacrifices the illustrious Rishabha installed his eldest son Bharata as the lord of the earth and went to the hermitage of Pulastya, being bent upon practising religious penance according to the prescribed rites of an anchoret. He practised religious austerities duly until he was so reduced as to be but a collection of skin and fibres. Thereupon putting a pebble in his mouth he went naked to the great road. And from then the country was handed over to Bharata by his father on retiring to woods and it was called Bhārata.

Bharata had a highly pious son named Sumati. Having ruled the kingdom for some time, the king Bharata, who was fond of sacrifices, conferred it upon his son and invested him with all royal splendours. O Muni, having engaged in austere practices, he renounced his life at the holy place of Salagrama. He was again born in a distinguished family of ascetics, which I shall describe to you later on.

From the illustrious Sumati was born Indradyumna: his son was Pratihara, who had an illustrious son named Pratihartta; his son was Bhava who begot Udgitha, who begot Prastara, whose son was Prithu. Prithu's son was Nakta, whose son was Gaya, whose son was Nara, whose son was Virat. Virat's son was the brave Dhimat who begot Maharta, whose son was Manasyu, whose son was Twashtri, whose son was Viraja, whose son was Raja, whose son was Satyjit, who had a hundred sons, of whom Viswagyotish was the eldest. Under the rule of these princes Bharatvarsha was divided into nine parts and their progeny successively ruled the country for seventy-one cycles.
O Muni, this was the progeny of Swayambhava Manu, by whom the earth was peopled, who was the lord of the first Manwantara in the Kalpa of Varaha.
